_note: Written by Claude as a stand-in for the Ollama model, in the same JSON format, to preview AI illustration. Not qwen3 output.

1.title: Security group inbound sources
1.explain: A security group rule's source can be an IP address, a CIDR range, a prefix list or another security group. An internet gateway is a VPC route target, not a traffic source, so its ID can't be used in a rule.

wrong.name: Security group as source
wrong.why: Valid: rules can reference another security group.

wrong.name: CIDR block range
wrong.why: Valid: a CIDR range is a normal rule source.

wrong.name: Single IP address
wrong.why: Valid: one IP with a /32 prefix works.

1.takeaway: Sources: IP, CIDR, prefix list, security group. Never a gateway.

2.title: Kinesis Data Streams for custom processing
2.explain: Kinesis Data Streams stores the stream so many custom consumers can read and replay it in real time. That decouples producers from your own processing apps, which is exactly what the company wants to build.

wrong.name: Kinesis Data Firehose
wrong.why: Only loads data into stores; no custom app processing.

wrong.name: Amazon SQS
wrong.why: A message queue, not a real-time stream for analytics.

wrong.name: Amazon SNS
wrong.why: Pub/sub notifications; can't replay or process streams.

2.takeaway: Custom real-time stream processing means Kinesis Data Streams.

3.title: StackSets across accounts and Regions
3.explain: A StackSet takes one CloudFormation template from the administrator account and creates stacks in many accounts and Regions in a single operation, so every department gets the same EC2 types and IAM roles.

wrong.name: CloudFormation templates
wrong.why: A template alone deploys nowhere; it needs a stack.

wrong.name: AWS RAM
wrong.why: Shares existing resources; it doesn't deploy templates.

wrong.name: CloudFormation stacks
wrong.why: One stack is one account and Region only.

3.takeaway: Many accounts plus many Regions means StackSets.

4.title: Restrict CloudFront to supplier IPs
4.explain: AWS WAF on the CloudFront distribution lets only the supplier IP ranges in. The origin access identity plus the bucket policy means S3 answers only CloudFront, so nobody can skip the WAF by going to S3 directly.

wrong.name: Security group on CloudFront
wrong.why: Security groups attach to instances, not CloudFront.

wrong.name: NACL on CloudFront
wrong.why: NACLs work on VPC subnets, not edge locations.

wrong.name: WAF on S3 bucket policy
wrong.why: WAF can't be attached to an S3 bucket policy.

4.takeaway: Filter at the edge with WAF; lock S3 to CloudFront.

5.title: Serverless static asset delivery
5.explain: S3 stores the static files with no servers to provision and scales on its own. CloudFront caches them at edge locations near players, so downloads are fast and the origin isn't hit for every request.

wrong.name: Lambda + RDS
wrong.why: A database isn't needed to serve static files.

wrong.name: Lambda + ElastiCache + RDS
wrong.why: Costly and complex for plain static downloads.

wrong.name: CloudFront + DynamoDB
wrong.why: DynamoDB is overkill; S3 is cheaper for files.

5.takeaway: Static content at scale: S3 origin behind CloudFront.

6.title: Global Accelerator static IPs
6.explain: Global Accelerator gives two static anycast IP addresses for the whole application. Each Region's Application Load Balancers sit behind its endpoints, so the firewall only needs those two IPs.

wrong.name: Elastic IP on Auto Scaling
wrong.why: You can't assign an Elastic IP to an Auto Scaling group.

wrong.name: NLB in front of ALBs
wrong.why: Still one NLB per Region; many IPs to manage.

wrong.name: Elastic IPs on each ALB
wrong.why: An ALB can't have an Elastic IP.

6.takeaway: Fewer IPs for many Regions: Global Accelerator.

1: An AWS documentation list of allowed security group rule sources: a single IPv4 or IPv6 address, a CIDR range, a prefix list ID, or another security group. An internet gateway is not on the list.
2: Kinesis Data Streams in the middle: producers send data in, and custom apps on Kinesis Data Analytics, Spark on EMR, EC2 or Lambda process it before analytics tools.
Kinesis Data Firehose loads streaming data into destinations such as Amazon S3, Redshift, Elasticsearch and Splunk, without custom processing apps.
3: An administrator account's StackSet creates the same stack in target accounts A and B, in each of two Regions.
6: A mobile device reaches AWS Global Accelerator on two static anycast IPs, which routes over the AWS global network to Network Load Balancers and EC2 instances in up to ten Regions.
